question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt this full multi-account configuration, setup, credential, authorization, and state contract as a supported public feature?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but it adds broad public configuration and upgrade-sensitive authentication and persisted-state behavior that requires explicit maintainer product ownership.

options.title: Sponsor the full account model
options.body: Accept the shared account architecture, legacy root compatibility, and per-account policy, auth, and state contract after the final check completes.

options.title: Narrow the initial release
options.body: Ask for a smaller first PR limited to bot identity, routing, and delivery while deferring delegated auth or stateful account features.

options.title: Do not sponsor now
options.body: Keep the canonical feature issue open and pause this implementation until maintainers want to own the full contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the full account model
recommendation.body: Accept the shared account architecture, legacy root compatibility, and per-account policy, auth, and state contract after the final check completes.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history is strongest across the Teams plugin, channel setup, and shared config/account surfaces affected by this product choice.
